questions.prompt: GetSystemVolumeWithDeviceType tries: (1) exact device+stream match, (2) SPEAKER fallback, (3) the final `return 0.5f` shown above. The unit test GetSystemVolumeWithDeviceType_Fallback_002 queries STREAM_ALARM on DEVICE_TYPE_EARPIECE with no prior SetSystemVolumeWithDeviceType call. The test comment says 'should return default 1.0f' but the assertion is `EXPECT_EQ(0.5f, result)`. What is the actual return value and why?

options.text: 1.0f — the comment is correct; the assertion is a typo that happens to pass because of floating-point comparison quirks
0.5f — the final fallback returns 0.5f, and since neither DEVICE_TYPE_EARPIECE nor DEVICE_TYPE_SPEAKER has STREAM_ALARM set, the code reaches that fallback
0.0f — an unset map entry defaults to 0.0f via std::map zero-initialization
Undefined behavior — reading from an unallocated map entry is UB

questions.explanation: deviceTypeToSystemVolumeMap_ is only populated with {DEVICE_TYPE_SPEAKER: {STREAM_MUSIC: 0.5f}} in the constructor. STREAM_ALARM is never set for any device. The lookup chain: find(DEVICE_TYPE_EARPIECE) fails -> find(DEVICE_TYPE_SPEAKER) succeeds but find(STREAM_ALARM) in the SPEAKER map fails -> falls through to `return 0.5f`. The code returns 0.5f; the test comment saying '1.0f' is misleading but the assertion is correct.
questions.reinforce: Correct — the fallback chain reaches 0.5f, not 1.0f as the comment claims.

questions.prompt: Two maps coexist in this constructor. SystemVolumeMap_ defaults STREAM_MUSIC to 1.0f; deviceTypeToSystemVolumeMap_ defaults SPEAKER+STREAM_MUSIC to 0.5f. Under EnhancedRouting, EffectDspVolumeUpdate calls GetSystemVolumeWithDeviceType (uses deviceTypeToSystemVolumeMap_) instead of GetSystemVolume (uses SystemVolumeMap_). Before any SetSystemVolumeWithDeviceType call, what volume does a SPEAKER+STREAM_MUSIC session get under EnhancedRouting vs. without EnhancedRouting?

options.text: EnhancedRouting: 1.0f, non-EnhancedRouting: 1.0f — both maps are initialized identically
EnhancedRouting: 0.5f, non-EnhancedRouting: 1.0f — the two maps have different defaults for the same logical concept
EnhancedRouting: 0.0f, non-EnhancedRouting: 1.0f — the device-typed map is empty until explicitly set
Both return 0.5f — SystemVolumeMap_ is no longer used at all

questions.explanation: deviceTypeToSystemVolumeMap_ is initialized with {DEVICE_TYPE_SPEAKER: {STREAM_MUSIC: 0.5f}}, so GetSystemVolumeWithDeviceType(STREAM_MUSIC, DEVICE_TYPE_SPEAKER) returns 0.5f. SystemVolumeMap_ is initialized with {STREAM_MUSIC: 1.0f}, so GetSystemVolume(STREAM_MUSIC) returns 1.0f. The same SPEAKER+MUSIC session gets different default volumes depending on the routing mode — a potential inconsistency to be aware of.
questions.reinforce: Correct — 0.5f vs 1.0f for the same logical default; the maps disagree.

questions.prompt: Under EnhancedRouting, GetOffloadEnabled() unconditionally returns false. Combined with the EffectVolumeUpdateInner change (Q1, which now calls both DSP and AP unconditionally), what is the net effect on the DSP volume update path under EnhancedRouting?

options.text: EffectDspVolumeUpdate is skipped because GetOffloadEnabled() returns false, so only AP volume update runs

EffectDspVolumeUpdate still runs because EffectVolumeUpdateInner no longer checks GetOffloadEnabled() — it calls both paths regardless, but inside EffectDspVolumeUpdate the offload-enabled sessions are filtered out
EffectDspVolumeUpdate crashes because it expects offload to be enabled when called
GetOffloadEnabled() returning false has no connection to EffectDspVolumeUpdate — they are independent code paths

questions.explanation: EffectVolumeUpdateInner no longer consults GetOffloadEnabled() at all — it calls both EffectDspVolumeUpdate and EffectApVolumeUpdate unconditionally. GetOffloadEnabled() returning false under EnhancedRouting means that inside EffectDspVolumeUpdate, the per-session offload checks (which use GetOffloadEnabled or device-specific offload flags) will report offload as disabled, so DSP volume logic runs but treats sessions as non-offloaded. The two changes work together: the gate moved from the caller to the callee.
questions.reinforce: Correct — the offload gate moved from EffectVolumeUpdateInner into the per-session logic of the DSP/AP update functions.
